question.text: 'Lotus Capital AIF' (Cat II) has raised total capital commitments of INR 200 crore. The manager issues a capital call ('drawdown') of 15% of commitments for a debt investment. Mr. Ramesh Iyer has committed INR 12 crore to the fund. How much must he wire on this drawdown?

explanation.text: The Logic: Drawdown pro-ration: each LP contributes in the ratio of his commitment. For Mr. Iyer: 15% x INR 12 crore = INR 1.80 crore. The fund-level pool draw is 15% x INR 200 crore = INR 30 crore, of which his share is 12/200 x 30 = INR 1.80 crore. The Trap: INR 1.20 cr is 10% (wrong pct). INR 1.50 cr is 12.5%. INR 2.00 cr is 16.67% or a rounding trap. Note: The workbook supports drawdown notices/capital calls and pro-rata investor rights by commitment. Notice-period market-practice commentary has been removed as it is not directly supported.
